Hi Rachel / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is Amaris' consolidated redline for the DPA and the Order Form (file: Amaris_DPA_redline_20260620.docx). We reviewed Redwood's MSA and the draft order form and have three items we'd like your position on before we route to procurement for final signoff: 

1) Risk allocation for data incidents (MSA §7 / DPA §4): our legal team prefers a bilateral cap carveout for confirmed data breaches tied to negligence thresholds. We highlighted proposed language in the redline.

2) SCCs and transfer addendum: we need confirmation on which SCC set Redwood intends to incorporate (EU Commission 2021 standard clauses vs updated annex approach) and whether you will accept our suggested controller-processor roles in the transfer addendum.

3) KMS / key separation and subprocessor list timing: we asked for KMS options and a current subprocessor snapshot. Our security team needs this for their procurement checklist.

We'd like to get clarity by end of day Friday if possible — Amaris is aiming to send the package to procurement early next week. Can you confirm who on Redwood will be the primary legal touch and whether a short triage call today is possible?

Thanks,
Samir Patel

Samir — appreciate the clear redline. I reviewed Amaris' edits and pulled the practical items into the attached summary (OrderForm_Amaris_Redline.pdf) to keep the triage tight. High-level positions below: 

1) Incident liability / cap carveout (MSA §7, DPA §4)
- Redwood is open to a narrowly framed carveout for confirmed data breaches caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct. 
- We cannot accept an unlimited carveout tied to "confirmable" incidents without a causation threshold. Proposed compromise language: "In the event of a Security Incident caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, Redwood's liability shall be subject to the lesser of (a) the liability cap in the MSA and (b) direct verified damages attributable to the incident." (see attached redline with highlight).

2) SCCs / transfer addendum
- Redwood intends to adopt the EU Commission 2021 Standard Contractual Clauses (Processor to Controller) plus a short transfer addendum mapping roles. We will not accept Amaris' suggested reclassification of processor/controller roles as that creates reciprocal obligations we cannot carry. Karthik will provide the exact text and a short note on subprocessors and transfer impact.

3) KMS / subprocessor list
- We can provide a current subprocessor snapshot and KMS architecture note (supporting HSM/KMS integrations) within one business day. Subprocessor disclosures will be provided in our standard CSV and updated prior to go-live.

Action: attaching our annotated DPA redline and an Order Form summary. If Amaris can confirm acceptance of the proposed liability threshold language above, we can aim to finalize commercial order form terms and route to DocuSign next week.

If helpful I can jump on the 2:00pm PT window Rachel suggested.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

Thanks Rachel / Laura — helpful and pragmatic. A couple quick clarifications before we route to procurement: 

• On the carveout wording: Amaris can accept the gross negligence / willful misconduct threshold but requests a short defined process (forensics, third-party verification) before liability flows. Can Redwood agree to a 30-day verification window and to cooperate with a mutually agreed forensics provider if requested?

• SCCs: thanks for confirming the 2021 SCCs. We just need confirmation that Redwood will accept a controller-to-processor mapping in the addendum and that any future changes to SCCs will be treated as administrative (mutual notice) and not trigger re-signing.

• DocuSign timeline: procurement wants to know if Redwood can send the final DocuSign package by Friday 6/26 if we lock language this week. That timeline would allow Amaris to finish procurement review the following week.

If usual for Redwood: happy to do a 15-minute verification call tomorrow AM (our time) for the verification process bullet and Karthik's SCCs note. Otherwise we can proceed over email.

Best,
Samir
